title: From Table to Cell: Attention for Better Reasoning with TABALIGN
claim: Existing planners and verifiers ignore cell grounding and fail at planning and reasoning; our approach fixes both bottlenecks together.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right: task, two bottlenecks, solution; warning icons vs green check
description: Four rounded, color-coded panels run left to right. The blue panel shows a table and the question "What is the average profit of all non-total costs?", plus a target icon listing the required steps. The red panel, "Bottleneck 1: Left-to-right bias", has a warning icon. It shows an autoregressive token order arrow and two column-permuted tables marked "Same semantics". Below them is a three-step plan with a red X for a wrong step. The orange panel, "Bottleneck 2: Unverified intermediate attention", shows a table with the relevant cells highlighted green. Beneath it is a red heatmap of wrong agent attention. The green panel, "TABALIGN addresses both bottlenecks", stacks three icon cards: Diffusion planner, AR executor and TABATTN verifier. A trophy box at the bottom reads "More reliable multi-turn table reasoning". The eye goes first to the red warning headers.
caption: Existing methods leave the cell-grounding contract implicit, producing failures at both planning and reasoning stages. At planning time, AR models impose an order-sensitive prior that conflicts with table permutation invariance, producing a globally inconsistent plan. At reasoning time, content-based PRMs score the generated state alone, leaving cell grounding to chance. TABALIGN operationalizes the contract through a diffusion-based bidirectional planner and the TABATTN verifier.
abstract: Multi-step LLM reasoning over structured tables fails because planning and execution share no explicit cell-grounding contract. Existing methods constrain the planner to a left-to-right factorization at odds with table permutation invariance, and score intermediate states by generated content alone, overlooking cell grounding. We conduct a pilot study showing that diffusion language models (DLMs) produce more human-aligned and permutation-stable cell attention on tables than autoregressive models, with a 40.2% median reduction in attention-AUROC variability under row reordering. Motivated by this, we propose TABALIGN, a planned table reasoning framework that operationalizes the contract. TABALIGN pairs a masked DLM planner, whose bidirectional denoising emits plan steps as binary cell masks, with TABATTN, a lightweight verifier trained on 1,600 human-verified attention standards to score each step by its attention overlap with the plan-designated mask. Across eight benchmarks covering table question answering and fact verification, TABALIGN improves average accuracy by 15.76 percentage points over the strongest open-source baseline at comparable 8B-class scale, with a matched-backbone ablation attributing 2.87 percentage points of this gain to the DLM planner over an AR planner on a fixed reasoner. Cleaner DLM plans also accelerate downstream reasoning execution by 44.64%.
